epa-historical.readScope: Complete two-page extracted May 1996 fact-sheet text read; no original page images viewed.

mill.sourceSummary: The provider describes a 1794 water-powered mill: controlled water flow turns a wheel linked to grinding stones for food production.
mill.attributionLimits: This selected historical machine changes work in its named community; a mechanical benefit does not establish the justice or overall impact of a colonial institution.
mill.question: Trace the provider-described water-to-wheel-to-stones route. Explain how grinding grain into flour serves a daily food need and how it changes the work compared with an original supplied hand-grinding alternative. Identify a benefit and dependence on water supply/maintenance; do not invent hours saved.
mill.expectedEvidence: Connect moving water, rotating parts and grinding purpose to preparation of food for people in this particular historical setting. Explain a plausible work change as an inference, separating that from the actual account.
mill.nearMiss: Says water turns directly into flour, every water mill has the same arrangement or a useful machine proves every community member benefited equally.
mill.changedCase: In the original changed case the water supply is low: explain which mechanism/service may be limited and what further evidence is needed before comparing alternatives.

pump.sourceSummary: UNICEF describes a 2017 handpump installation near homes in Binginde Share and a 2018 account of easier daily water access, with a community maintenance arrangement.
pump.attributionLimits: Provider and named participant account, not a pupil health diagnosis, guarantee of present water safety or universal disability experience.
pump.question: Explain how an adult-operated handpump changes access to water used for washing/cooking in the specific community account. Compare its daily-work impact with the historical mill, naming both communities/dates and different purposes. Include why maintenance matters.
pump.expectedEvidence: Relate a human-operated mechanism to drawing water and a reported access benefit; separate less travel from an unproven claim that every illness disappeared. Compare food-processing and water-access needs across the two communities.
pump.nearMiss: Says a handpump makes contaminated water safe merely by moving it, or treats the 2018 report as proof of current universal conditions.
pump.changedCase: The original changed case has a broken handle or unavailable spare part: explain the access consequence and why a maintenance arrangement matters without claiming the studied pump actually failed.

mower-comparison.sourceSummary: EPA distinguishes petrol equipment emissions from manual and electric alternatives, including a manual reel mower for small lawns and generally quieter/lower-polluting electric equipment.
mower-comparison.attributionLimits: Original equal-task comparison, not a measured lifecycle study. A powered mower may meet a different capacity/access need; no pupil operates blades, batteries or fuel.
mower-comparison.question: Original fictional brief: the same small grass area must be maintained. Compare a manual reel mower, a battery-electric mower and a petrol mower that can each complete the specified job. Explain energy input, direct exhaust/noise and resource/material/maintenance questions; rank sustainability, function/accessibility, safety, cost and appearance with reasons. State what additional evidence a full manufacture-to-disposal comparison would need.
mower-comparison.expectedEvidence: Compare like purposes and stated capacity; petrol combustion produces local exhaust, electric operation avoids local fuel exhaust but electricity/battery production and disposal still matter, and a manual machine still uses materials and human effort. Justify a context-bound choice rather than call any option impact-free. Distinguish resource source from electricity as carrier.
mower-comparison.nearMiss: Chooses by colour alone, compares machines doing different jobs as though identical or says electric/manual means no environmental effect anywhere.
mower-comparison.changedCase: The original brief changes to a much larger steep site or a user who cannot safely push the manual machine: reconsider function/accessibility and evidence, rather than declare one universal winner or require an unsafe trial.

wholeClaimReview.readScope: All four complete direct cards read. Q2 mechanism and VI5 natural-resource saved guides read in full. Q2Zj and cOJ have no saved guides. Q2 hard closure remains as recorded in the mechanism dossier; cOJ to Q2Zj read.
limits: Existing mechanism claim retains actual force-effect/part/motion knowledge and safe real observation requirements; an impact explanation does not certify whole mechanism mastery.
Whole Things people design retains product, service and designed-environment examples; these two machines are contribution examples, not a replacement for that inventory.

Whole natural resources retains replenishment classification, fossil/fissile versus renewable distinctions and obtaining/combining resource information. The mower task contributes resource/environment reasoning, not all whole-topic evidence.
Design factors are actually compared/ranked for a supplied brief, with changed needs and trade-offs. No old claim, guide, age or edge is narrowed or lowered.

safety: Information and original fictional brief only. No real pump water consumption/quality testing, mill mechanism access, mower operation, blades, fuel handling or battery modification. No personal health or disability disclosure.
